page: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the Xen hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, supplying 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 15 GB of system memory, yielding 1.88 GB per vCPU, alongside 160 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Vector extensions are limited to standard AVX and AES instructions, with newer instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AMX unsupported.

Benchmark evaluations reveal performance limitations characteristic of legacy Ivy Bridge-EP architectures. Single-core performance is constrained, scoring 717.0 in Geekbench single-core and 1280.58 in stress-ng. Multi-threaded throughput achieves moderate results, reaching 6681.49 in stress-ng and 7237.82 in PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains competitive for cached operations at 388.0 GB/sec for small blocks, but drops to 50.08 GB/sec for large uncached reads. Clang compilation and static web serving tests deliver mid-tier results, whereas modern instruction-dependent tasks such as 7B LLM text generation perform poorly at 5.17 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the c3.2xlarge offers dedicated execution cores and high-speed local scratch storage on older hardware. While newer generations provide superior performance per watt and advanced vector instructions, this instance provides predictable compute for legacy workloads. It is functionally suited for batch processing, build automation, static web servers, and compilation pipelines that benefit from direct local SSD storage but do not require modern vector acceleration.
description: Amazon Web Services c3.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 processor running at 2.8 GHz under the Xen hypervisor. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 15 GB of RAM (1.88 GB per vCPU), and 160 GB of local SSD scratch storage with a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Compute benchmarks demonstrate moderate multi-core throughput alongside weaker single-core scores, as shown by its PassMark CPU score of 7237.82 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2782.0. With hardware instruction sets limited to legacy AVX and AES, the instance lacks AVX-512 and modern AI vector optimizations. The c3.2xlarge is practical for intermediate multi-threaded batch operations, software builds, continuous integration pipelines, and static web serving where bundled local disk space is advantageous.
